Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Money, work & business

total noun and adjective

the whole amount, added up

also in total, in all, altogether, the total, sum total, the total cost, the total number

classical

Plaut. Mil. 46: Quanta istaec hominum summast?
Cic. Att. 5.21.11: subdūcāmus summam
Cic. Off. 1.59 (Lewis & Short)

summa, summae f.

noun, first declension

the total, the sum

Of a reckoning, the sum of all the items (Lewis & Short). To work out the total is summam subdūcere or summam facere; a total sum of money, summa pecūniae (Liv. 30.16.12, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • omnīnō — in total, in all, altogether

    adverb · classical · Caes. BG 1.6: Erant omnīnō itinera duo; Cic. Clu. 76: quīnque omnīnō fuērunt (Lewis & Short); Traupman 119: Omnīnō quattuor cubicula, four bedrooms in all

Examples

  • Quanta istaec hominum summast? — Septem mīlia. — Tantum esse oportet. rēctē ratiōnem tenēs.

    What’s the total number of men? — Seven thousand. — That’s what it should be; your sums are right.Plaut. Mil. 46–47

  • Erant omnīnō itinera duo, quibus itineribus domō exīre possent

    there were only two routes in all by which they could leave homeCaes. BG 1.6

  • rēctē inquit Scaptius, sed subdūcāmus summam

    ‘Fine,’ says Scaptius, ‘but let’s add up the total’Cic. Att. 5.21.11

See also total, count, add, money, whole.
